rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The world's loudest language Sport needs no translation: a last-minute goal means the same thing in Kathmandu and São Paulo. That shared heartbeat is exactly why the theme teaches English so well — you already have the passion, and the unit supplies the register: the crisp facts of the match report, the moral vocabulary of fair play, the argument frames for money in sport.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Sports vocabulary (tournament, referee, endurance) appears in gap-fills — revise it.
Argument answers: sports build discipline and unity; give one counterpoint too.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## The argument at the heart of the game Every interesting sports essay is the same tension in different clothes: the game promises **fair play** and pays for **winning**. Doping, match-fixing and gamesmanship are what the tension looks like when it goes wrong; sportsmanship is what it looks like when it goes right. Hold both sides and you write the best answers.…  ·  ## The comparison the exam favours | Basis | Individual sport | Team sport | | --- | --- | --- | | Examples | athletics, swimming, martial arts, chess | football, cricket, volleyball | | Responsibility | wholly yours — nowhere to hide | distributed across roles | | Motivation | self-driven, solitary hours | peer-driven, coached | | Failure | private and total | shared and partial | | Fame | the person is the brand |…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## How the exam asks it The **match report** (6–8 marks) gives you notes and wants the five-fact lead, the turning point, one passive, one quote. Checklist the five facts before writing the lead — structure marks are the cheapest on the paper.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. What values does playing sport build? (2 marks) — discipline and teamwork; one sentence each with an example.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Q. Why should schools invest in sports? (2 marks) — physical health plus concentration and character; link to academics.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The words that carry the theme Match-day English is a working vocabulary, not a list. **Events and people:** tournament, league, fixture, semi-final, tie-breaker, draw; athlete, coach, umpire, referee, spectator, captain, substitute.…  ·  ## Reading the theme like a writer — the report and the commentary A **match report** is journalism in miniature, and its shape is fixed: a headline that moves; a **lead paragraph** carrying the five facts — who won, against whom, by what margin, where, when; a body that walks the match in order and pauses at the turning point; a reaction from the captain or coach; and a last line pointing forward.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Sports passages are stat-heavy — mark numbers, names and superlatives; factual questions target them directly.  ·  Trick 2: Essay questions on sports: pick the values angle (discipline, teamwork, health) and argue with one real example, not a list.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Why should schools invest in sports? (2 marks) — physical health plus concentration and character; link to academics.
